ops.text: `ccx vcs ship` refuses with "multiple nearest bookmarks \"main, worktree-A, worktree-B, worktree-C\"; pass --branch <name> to choose one" — and passing --branch main does not help. Neither does --bookmark main, its documented jj-only alias. Both produce the identical error, so the message prescribes a remedy that does not work: the nearest-bookmark resolution runs before, or independently of, the flag that is supposed to disambiguate it. Reproduced twice in cc-notes with `ccx vcs ship --branch main -m ... <paths>` and `ccx vcs ship --bookmark main -m ... --no-pr <path>`, ccx as of 2026-07-30. The setup that triggers it is ordinary and getting more common: three Workflow `isolation: 'worktree'` worktrees, each on its own git branch, all still sitting on the same commit as main because none has committed yet — so `@-` carries four bookmarks. Cost was the whole ship lane: no prek gate, no CI watch, no PR handling, and the fallback is hand-rolling `jj describe` / `jj new` / `jj bookmark set main -r @-` / `jj git push --bookmark main` plus running `uvx prek run --files ...` and `gh run watch` separately — which also loses ship's fetch-rebase-retry, and I hit exactly that race on the first push (the guides bot had advanced main mid-work). Deleting the worktree bookmarks is not an out while a workflow is live in one of them: they are the worktrees' checked-out branches. Either --branch should be honored by that resolution, or the error should name the mechanism that actually disambiguates.
